title: Cross-Org Objective Backbone and Initiative Attribution Framework
creator: Mariana Gomez
description: Create a pragmatic, machine-readable backbone that maps company-level objectives to owning initiatives across Product, Engineering, Design, and GTM. The framework must support automated rollups for executive reporting, detect orphaned initiatives, and enable initiative attribution so teams can report contribution to OKR key results without manual spreadsheets. Deliverables: (1) an initiative schema (minimal fields), (2) a tagging and ownership convention, (3) a lightweight ingestion pipeline from Linear and Google Sheets, and (4) a dashboard spec for the Executive Roadmap view.
background: Current state: teams maintain siloed initiative lists and multiple ad-hoc spreadsheets for OKR rollups. Quarter handoffs create mismatched initiative scopes and duplicated work. Prior PM audits found ~17% of initiatives without clear KR alignment and several duplicated efforts across infra and console teams. Leadership requested a single source of truth with low friction for teams to adopt.
goals: Define a minimal initiative schema that supports automated mapping to company OKRs
Enable per-initiative attribution (primary owner + contributing teams + estimated impact)
Ship an ingest adapter for Linear issues and shared Google Sheet templates
Launch an Executive Roadmap dashboard with drill-down to initiative level and change history
acceptance_criteria: Schema spec published and reviewed by Eng, Design, and Security
Automated ingest successfully maps 95% of existing initiatives with no manual mapping
Executive dashboard shows live rollups and highlights orphaned initiatives
Onboarding doc and two training sessions run with 20+ PM/Eng leads
milestones: 2025-02-28: Draft schema and tagging convention v0
2025-03-07: Engineering spike for ingestion pipeline (Linear -> schema)
2025-03-21: Beta ingest run and executive dashboard prototype
risks: Low adoption if schema is too heavy — mitigated by minimal required fields and auto-population
Ingest errors due to inconsistent Linear naming conventions — mitigated by a mapping UI for edge cases
Disagreement on ownership granularity across orgs — mitigated via tolerance for multi-owner attribution and a primary-owner rule
Dashboard performance on large datasets — addressed by caching and incremental syncs
decision_log: 2025-02-25 — Decided to keep schema minimal: required fields = key, title, primary_owner, aligned_okrs, phase, estimated_impact. Optional fields allowed for notes/attachments.
2025-03-05 — Chose Linear as canonical ingestion source; Google Sheet adapter only for partner orgs that cannot use Linear.
2025-03-09 — Trade-off: normalized KR alignment vs. flexible tagging. We will accept free-text KRs but normalize at ingest using a fuzzy-matching step and a human review queue.
2025-03-11 — Approved rollout cadence: pilot (2 weeks) -> widen to 6 teams -> company-wide adoption next quarter.

notes: Plan emphasizes low-friction adoption: minimal required fields, auto-mapping, and a small human review step. Pilot will focus on infra, console, and platform PMs to validate cross-functional behavior before expanding. If adoption lags, we'll run a weekly sync and provide PM-specific incentives (quarterly OKR credit).
approval: 2025-03-11 — Exec sponsors (CTO, VP Product) approved pilot. Proceed to Beta ingest and dashboard prototype.
post_mortem_plan: If rollout misses adoption targets (70% of target teams in 6 weeks), schedule a 2-week retro to collect blockers, iterate schema, and add automation for manual steps.
communication_plan: Announcement to company via All-Hands + TL notes
Team-specific training: 2 live sessions and a recorded walkthrough
Update PM onboarding docs and include template in PM toolkit
